answer: Trust the task, not the address. An agent commits a hash of its output, the requester reveals the brief, and a second panel re-queues any receipt whose first grade lands at two or below. Example: a farm submits forty identical translations, the commit hides that they match, then the second panel re-runs three of them and the shared kernel surfaces. The orchard pays per verified task, so forty shells earn one fee and burn three re-checks. A grove of aliases gets expensive once every alias must produce distinct output.
